standard_prerequisites.name: Telescoping of binomial coefficients

standard_prerequisites.use: The adjusted combination has zero difference, which forces g to be eventually constant.

core_obligations: Write the difference f(n) - f(n-1) as a sum of binomial coefficients with integer coefficients, valid for all large n (proof line 14079).
Subtract the telescoping combination from f to get a function g whose difference vanishes for all large n, hence g is eventually constant, say equal to a_{-1} (proof lines 14080-14083).

Rewrite f as that constant plus the telescoping combination; the author leaves the final check that this has the required binomial shape to the reader, pointing at a remark above the lemma (proof lines 14083-14086).
proof_roadmap: Subtract an antiderivative built from binomial coefficients so that the difference dies (proof lines 14078-14082).
Conclude the adjusted function is eventually constant and reassemble f (proof lines 14082-14087).
difficulty_reason: The lemma states that an eventually defined function f with numerical-polynomial difference is itself a numerical polynomial (statement lines 14069-14076). The proof does not interpolate or use finite differences of higher order: it sums the given binomial expansion of the difference to build the telescoping function g(n) = f(n) minus the shifted binomial combination, observes that g has zero difference for large n and is therefore eventually constant, and rewrites f as that constant plus the combination (proof lines 14078-14087). The construction of the telescoping term is the substance; the final check of the required shape is left to the reader by a sentence that is kept verbatim inside the span. H2.
